title: The tracker and the gate both name their worktree 'tree', and race
description:
CI failed on a TypeScript-only branch with a git worktree race:

    reconcile_observer_test.go:107: the run ended under observation: reconcile: prepare the
    tracker's worktree on epic/qeu: git worktree add --detach --quiet /tmp/ticfac-tracker-2270000979/tree
    22006bc4c280: exit status 128: fatal: could not open '.git/worktrees/tree/locked' for
    writing: No such file or directory

Mechanism: git registers a worktree under .git/worktrees/<basename of the path>. Two places create worktrees whose directory is named exactly `tree`:

    internal/reconcile/git.go:244      dir = filepath.Join(root, "tree")     the tracker's checkout
    internal/reconcile/gatedir.go:125  tree := filepath.Join(held, "tree")   the gate slot (tick 6wh)

So both register as `tree`. Git picks a free name (tree, tree1, tree2 ...) and then creates the directory, and those two steps are not atomic: two concurrent `worktree add` calls can both decide `tree` is free, and the loser finds the administrative directory gone from under it while writing `locked`.

6wh made this much more likely. Before it, gate runs used a throwaway worktree with a random directory name; now every gate slot ends in /tree, so a repository's gate and its tracker collide by construction whenever they overlap - which on a wave-width-4 run is most of the time.

Not caused by the branch it failed on (a TypeScript-only change); main is green on the same commit, which is what a race looks like.

Fix shape: give each worktree a name that cannot collide, rather than a shared one. `git worktree add` takes the path, and the registration name follows the basename - so name the directories for what they are and who owns them (tracker-<run id>, gate-slot-<n>) instead of all calling them `tree`. Check whether anything depends on the basename being `tree`; the gate's redaction test (TestAFailingGatesOutputCarriesNoHostPath) knows about these paths.

A guard is worth having: a test that creates the tracker worktree and a gate slot concurrently against one repository and asserts both succeed. It would have caught this when 6wh landed.

Found by CI on PR #22.
acceptance_criteria: The tracker worktree and a gate slot can be created concurrently against one repository without either failing, proven by a test that does exactly that and fails on the shared name
